title: Ethiopian Lamb Shoulder Tibs
community: Ethiopian restaurants — the bone-in lamb shoulder tibs
author: Chef Haile
desc: Ethiopian Lamb Shoulder Tibs — bone-in lamb shoulder pieces sautéed in kibbeh with jalapeño, rosemary, onion, and tomato. More gelatinous and flavourful than boneless lamb tibs — the collagen from the shoulder bones enriches the pan sauce.
longDesc: Shoulder tibs uses the bone-in shoulder rather than the tender leg cuts — the result is a richer, more complex tibs where the collagen from the bone enriches the pan sauce. It requires slightly longer cooking but the flavour reward is significant.
ingredients: 700g bone-in lamb shoulder — chopped through the bone into pieces
steps: Sear lamb shoulder pieces on all sides — 3 minutes.
Add garlic, jalapeño, rosemary, berbere, and tomatoes.
Cook 5—8 more minutes — the bone-in pieces need more time than boneless.
Season. The pan sauce should be slightly more gelatinous than standard tibs.
chefTips: Bone-in lamb shoulder pieces — the specific cut.
Slightly longer cooking than boneless tibs — the bone conducts heat more slowly.
commonMistakes: Expecting it to cook as fast as boneless tibs.
cookingScience: Bone-in cooking releases collagen and marrow from the bone surface — these dissolve into the pan sauce as the cooking progresses, producing the characteristic slightly sticky, gelatinous sauce.
sustainabilityTips: Shoulder is a secondary cut — more sustainable use of the whole animal.
healthBenefits: Collagen from bone adds joint-supporting gelatin.
culturalNote: Shoulder tibs is the tibs of the knowledgeable Ethiopian restaurant-goer — ordered for the richer, more complex flavour that only bone-in cooking can produce.
